evals.prompt: It's been a few months since rulegate setup and we've bolted a handful of new lines onto CLAUDE.md since. Audit my rules before I trust them again.
evals.expected_behavior: Invokes rules-audit standalone, per "Runnable any time as a drift check." Runs the six checks (atomicity, observability, vague quantifiers, resolvable references, dead weight, contradiction) against at least the newly added rules -- fast mode is acceptable, full re-audit if structure may have rotted -- and returns the one-table verdict output. Does not require going through rulegate-setup to run.

evals.prompt: Are my rules enforceable? I want to know before I have the agent classify them into SEQUENCING/SCOPE/etc.
evals.expected_behavior: Invokes rules-audit; "are my rules enforceable" is a direct trigger phrase. Evaluates each rule against the requirement/acceptance-criterion/process-instruction bar and returns the full verdict table (enforceable/rewritable/judgment/dead/contradiction) before any classification happens.

evals.prompt: Move the plan marker to step 2, the failing test for the auth bug is in place now.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not invoke rules-audit. This is advancing an already-classified plan (a SEQUENCING rule already satisfied by step order) -- a rule-compiler action, not a question about whether any rule is well-formed.

evals.prompt: Remind me what the difference is between a SCOPE rule and a STYLE rule in rulegate.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not invoke rules-audit. This asks for an explanation of the shape taxonomy, not an evaluation of specific project rules for enforceability -- there is no rule text supplied or referenced to render a verdict on.

evals.prompt: Let's get rulegate set up for this project -- here's my CLAUDE.md.
evals.expected_behavior: Judgment call. This is rulegate-setup's own trigger phrase, and rulegate-setup step 3 makes running rules-audit mandatory before classification -- so the audit still happens, just dispatched by rulegate-setup rather than chosen independently by the model in direct response to this prompt. Whether that counts as rules-audit itself "triggering" on this input, or only rulegate-setup triggering with rules-audit following inside it, has no single correct read -- but either way, the same one-table audited verdict output must appear before any rule is classified. Skipping straight to classification without it fails regardless of which framing is used.
